title: org-lsp configuration
description: The options of the org-lsp server, in its shared configuration file. See docs/configuration.org.

org_agenda_files.description: Files, directories and glob patterns (`*`, `?`, `**`) the agenda is built from. `~/` is the home directory, and a directory stands for the Org files directly in it. When empty, the agenda is built from the Org files under the workspace folders (hidden directories, `node_modules` and `target` left out), or else from the Org files that are open. (`org-agenda-files`)

org_agenda_file_regexp.description: Which files of a directory in `org_agenda_files` are agenda files: an Emacs regular expression their names match, such as `\\.txt\\'` for the names that end in `.txt`. (`org-agenda-file-regexp`)

org_agenda_skip_unavailable_files.description: Leave out the files of `org_agenda_files` that are not there. With `false`, opening an agenda view asks about each: `r` removes it from the list until the server starts again, anything else aborts. (`org-agenda-skip-unavailable-files`)

org_todo_keywords.description: The TODO sequence, written like Org's `#+TODO:` line. `|` separates the states that count as done; without it the last keyword is the only done state. `TODO(t)` gives a keyword a key for fast selection, and `WAIT(w@/!)` makes it log a note (`@`) or the time (`!`) on entering and leaving it. Several sequences go in a list of lists, `[["TODO", "|", "DONE"], ["REPORT", "|", "FIXED"]]`; cycling stays in the sequence of the entry, and `C-S-<right>` switches to the next. A list that starts with `type` is a type sequence (`#+TYP_TODO:`): each of its keywords goes straight to done. A file's own `#+TODO:` lines take precedence. (`org-todo-keywords`)

org_todo_interpretation.description: What a list of keywords alone in `org_todo_keywords` is (Org's old syntax): a sequence, or types, each going straight to done. A list that starts with `sequence` or `type` says it itself. (`org-todo-interpretation`)

org_todo_keyword_faces.description: Faces for particular TODO keywords: a color, `{ "WAIT": "orange" }`, or attributes written as Org writes them, `{ "CANCELLED": ":foreground gray :slant italic :strike-through t" }` (`:foreground`, `:background`, `:weight bold`, `:slant italic`, `:underline t`, `:strike-through t`). Shown in Org files and in the agenda by Neovim, Vim and VS Code. (`org-todo-keyword-faces`)

org_priority_faces.description: Faces for particular priorities, by their letter, written as in `org_todo_keyword_faces`: `{ "A": ":foreground red :weight bold" }`. (`org-priority-faces`)

org_tag_faces.description: Faces for particular tags of headlines, written as in `org_todo_keyword_faces`: `{ "work": "orange" }`. Shown in Org files (not the agenda, as in Emacs) by Neovim, Vim and VS Code. (`org-tag-faces`)

org_log_done.description: Write `CLOSED:` with the time when an entry is done, and with `note` ask for a note too. A file's `#+STARTUP:` words `logdone`, `lognotedone` and `nologdone` change it there; an entry's `LOGGING` property (inherited) says what its state changes log instead: those words, `logrepeat` and its relatives, and keywords with what they log (`WAIT(@/!)`), or `nil` for nothing. (`org-log-done`)

org_log_repeat.description: Record when a repeating entry is done and moves to its next date. `#+STARTUP:` `logrepeat`, `lognoterepeat` and `nologrepeat` change it in a file, and the `LOGGING` property in an entry. (`org-log-repeat`)

org_M_RET_may_split_line.description: Inserting a heading, an item or a table row (M-RET) in the middle of a line splits it, the rest going to the new one; `false`: it goes in after the line. One by context: `{ "headline": false, "item": true, "table": true }`, `default` for those not named. (`org-M-RET-may-split-line`)

org_blank_before_new_entry.description: Whether a new heading (`heading`) and a new item (`plain_list_item`) get an empty line before them: `true`, `false`, or `"auto"`, as the headings or items around them have. (`org-blank-before-new-entry`)

org_insert_heading_respect_content.description: M-RET and M-S-RET outside lists put the new heading after the subtree, as C-RET does. (`org-insert-heading-respect-content`)

org_special_ctrl_a_e.description: How C-a and C-e (`org.beginning.of.line`, `org.end.of.line`) move on a headline or an item: `true` to the start of the headline's title, after the stars, TODO keyword and priority, or after the item's bullet and check-box, and to the end of the title, before the tags; the same key again to the line's own start or end. `reversed` goes to the line's start or end first, and to those places on the same key right after. A pair, as `[true, false]`, sets C-a and C-e apart. With `false` the key keeps the editor's own meaning. (`org-special-ctrl-a/e`)

org_sparse_tree_open_archived_trees.description: A sparse tree (`C-c /`, and a link's `/regexp/`) shows its matches in archived subtrees (tagged `ARCHIVE`); with `false` those subtrees stay folded under their headline. (`org-sparse-tree-open-archived-trees`)

org_occur_case_fold_search.description: Whether a sparse tree (`C-c /`, and a link's `/regexp/`) ignores case; `"smart"` ignores it unless what is searched for has an upper-case letter. (`org-occur-case-fold-search`)

org_highlight_sparse_tree_matches.description: Highlight the matches of a sparse tree (`C-c /`, and a link's `/regexp/`) until the text changes; with `false`, only their lines show. (`org-highlight-sparse-tree-matches`)

org_remove_highlights_with_change.description: The highlights of a sparse tree (`C-c /` by a regexp, TODO keywords or dates, and a link's `/regexp/`) and the times of `C-c C-x C-d` go at the next change of the text; with `false` they stay until `C-c C-c`. Those of a sparse tree by tags or a property always stay, as in Emacs. (`org-remove-highlights-with-change`)

org_sparse_tree_default_date_type.description: The timestamps the date sparse trees (`C-c /` `b`, `a`, `D`) look at first: `null` for scheduled and deadline dates, or one kind; `c` in the menu turns to the next kind. (`org-sparse-tree-default-date-type`)

org_yank_adjusted_subtrees.description: C-y (`org.yank`, Emacs keys) of one or more subtrees at the start of a line, or after the stars of an otherwise empty headline, pastes them as `org.paste.subtree` does: at the level of the headlines around them. Anything else is the editor's own paste. (`org-yank-adjusted-subtrees`)

org_yank_folded_subtrees.description: C-y (`org.yank`, Emacs keys) of one or more subtrees at the start of a line folds them, unless that would hide text after them (*Inserted text not folded because that would swallow text*), and leaves the cursor on the line after them. With `false` (and `org_yank_adjusted_subtrees` off) it is the editor's own paste. (`org-yank-folded-subtrees`)

org_allow_promoting_top_level_subtree.description: Promoting a headline of level 1 makes it a comment line: `# ` in place of `* `, its children a level up with a subtree's promotion. With `false` it is an error. (`org-allow-promoting-top-level-subtree`)

org_odd_levels_only.description: Only odd levels: `*`, `***`, `*****`, each counted as the next level. Promoting and demoting go two stars at a time, and a headline is colored and matched (`LEVEL`) by the level it counts as. `#+STARTUP: odd` and `oddeven` set it for a file. (`org-odd-levels-only`)

org_inlinetask_min_level.description: A headline of at least this many stars (twice as many less one with `org_odd_levels_only`) is an inline task: a task inside the text of its entry, closed by a line of as many stars and `END`. It is no part of the outline: it has no subtree, the outline and the motion between headings pass it, and it folds its text up to its `END` line. `false`: there are no inline tasks, as in Emacs before `org-inlinetask` is loaded. (`org-inlinetask-min-level`)

org_inlinetask_show_first_star.description: The stars of an inline task but the last two are hidden, as `org_hide_leading_stars` hides those of a headline; with `true` none are. (`org-inlinetask-show-first-star`)

org_inlinetask_default_state.description: The TODO keyword of a new inline task (`org.inlinetask.insert`). (`org-inlinetask-default-state`)

org_treat_S_cursor_todo_selection_as_sta.description: `S-<left>` and `S-<right>` on a headline change its TODO state as any change does: logged, and blocked by its dependencies. Off, they change it with nothing logged and nothing in the way. (`org-treat-S-cursor-todo-selection-as-state-change`)

org_treat_insert_todo_heading_as_state_c.description: The keyword of a heading `org.insert.todo.heading` (M-S-RET) makes is set as a TODO change: logged as the keyword says (a note wanted is a time only), with its tag triggers. (`org-treat-insert-todo-heading-as-state-change`)

org_edit_timestamp_down_means_later.description: `S-<down>` makes a timestamp later and `S-<up>` earlier, the other way round from Org's default. (`org-edit-timestamp-down-means-later`)

org_priority_enable_commands.description: Whether the priority commands work. With `false` they refuse (`Priority commands are disabled`), and `S-<up>` and `S-<down>` on a headline do not change its priority. (`org-priority-enable-commands`)

org_track_ordered_property_with_tag.description: A tag that `org.ordered.toggle` (`C-c C-x o`) puts on the headline with the `ORDERED` property and takes off without it: `true` for `ORDERED`, or a tag of your own. Only the property orders the subtasks. (`org-track-ordered-property-with-tag`)

org_special_ctrl_o.description: `org.open.line` (C-o) in a table inserts a row above; with `false` it opens a line there too. (`org-special-ctrl-o`)

org_special_ctrl_k.description: C-k (`org.kill.line`) on a headline kills the text to the tags, and the tags when the cursor is past the title; at the start of the line, the whole line. With `false` the key keeps the editor's own meaning, but on a line a closed fold starts on (see `org_ctrl_k_protect_subtree`). (`org-special-ctrl-k`)

org_ctrl_k_protect_subtree.description: C-k (`org.kill.line`) on a line a closed fold starts on (a headline's only from its start with `org_special_ctrl_k`) kills what the fold hides with the line, as Emacs's `kill-line` does: `true` asks first (*Kill hidden subtree along with headline?*), `"error"` refuses (*‘C-k’ aborted as it would kill a hidden subtree*), `false` kills. Needs an editor that says which folds are closed (not VS Code). (`org-ctrl-k-protect-subtree`)

org_list_allow_alphabetical.description: Whether a letter may stand for the number of an ordered item (`a.`, `B)`). A list of more than 26 items is numbered. (`org-list-allow-alphabetical`)

org_plain_list_ordered_item_terminator.description: What ends the number of an ordered item: `"."`, `")"`, or `true` for either. (`org-plain-list-ordered-item-terminator`)

org_list_two_spaces_after_bullet_regexp.description: An Emacs regexp: the bullets it matches get two spaces after them when Org writes them (a new item, a bullet changed, a list repaired). (`org-list-two-spaces-after-bullet-regexp`)

org_list_demote_modify_bullet.description: By bullet (`-`, `+`, `*`, `1.`, `1)`), the bullet an item gets when it is indented: `{ "+": "-", "-": "+" }`. (`org-list-demote-modify-bullet`)

org_list_indent_offset.description: How many more columns sub-items are indented, past their parent's bullet. (`org-list-indent-offset`)

org_list_automatic_rules.description: `checkbox`: the statistics cookies are counted again when a box changes, and colored as done or not. `indent`: indenting the first item of a list with its children (M-S-<right>) moves the whole list. A rule left out of the object is off. (`org-list-automatic-rules`)

org_checkbox_hierarchical_statistics.description: A checkbox cookie counts the boxes of the items right below it; `false` counts every box further down too, as `recursive` in a `COOKIE_DATA` property does. (`org-checkbox-hierarchical-statistics`)

org_table_number_regexp.description: An Emacs regexp: the fields it matches are numbers, and a column mostly of numbers aligns right. (`org-table-number-regexp`)

org_table_number_fraction.description: How much of a column's filled fields must be numbers for it to align right. (`org-table-number-fraction`)

org_table_automatic_realign.description: TAB and RET in a table align it before they move; `false`: only C-c C-c and the commands that change rows or columns do. (`org-table-automatic-realign`)

org_table_tab_jumps_over_hlines.description: TAB at the end of a row before a horizontal line goes to the row after it; `false`: it makes a row before the line. (`org-table-tab-jumps-over-hlines`)

org_table_shrunk_column_indicator.description: What shows at the end of each field of a shrunk column. (`org-table-shrunk-column-indicator`)

org_table_formula_constants.description: Constants for the table formulas of every file, by name: `{ "c": "299792458." }` gives `$c`. A file's `#+CONSTANTS:` come first. (`org-table-formula-constants`)

org_table_relative_ref_may_cross_hline.description: Whether a relative reference in a formula (`@-1`) goes past a horizontal line: `false` stops at the field next to it, `"error"` makes the formula fail. (`org-table-relative-ref-may-cross-hline`)

org_table_formula_create_columns.description: A field formula past the last column adds the columns it needs, rather than failing. (`org-table-formula-create-columns`)

org_table_duration_custom_format.description: How a formula with `;t` writes a duration: a number of seconds, minutes, hours or days, or hours and minutes. (`org-table-duration-custom-format`)

org_table_duration_hour_zero_padding.description: Durations of formulas (`;T`, `;U`) have their hours on two digits: `08:32:34` rather than `8:32:34`. (`org-table-duration-hour-zero-padding`)

org_calc_default_modes.description: The modes table formulas start with: `float_format`, `["float", digits]`, `["fix", decimals]` or `["sci", digits]`, and `angle_mode`, `"deg"` or `"rad"`. A formula's own modes (`;f2`) win; Calc's other modes are not offered. (`org-calc-default-modes`)

org_table_formula_evaluate_inline.description: TAB and RET on a field that is a formula (`=$1*2`, `:=...`) evaluate it, which org-lsp refuses (the formula goes in a `#+TBLFM:` line); `false` leaves the field as text. (`org-table-formula-evaluate-inline`)

org_table_allow_automatic_line_recalcula.description: TAB, RET and C-c C-c on a line marked `#` recalculate it. (`org-table-allow-automatic-line-recalculation`)

org_list_use_circular_motion.description: Moving to the next item from the last goes to the first, and back; moving the last item down puts it first, the first up puts it last. (`org-list-use-circular-motion`)

org_enforce_todo_dependencies.description: An entry cannot be done while a child is not, or, under a parent with the `ORDERED` property, while an earlier sibling is not: the change is refused with what blocks it. (`org-enforce-todo-dependencies`)

org_agenda_dim_blocked_tasks.description: Dim the tasks of the agenda and the TODO list that their dependencies keep from being done (with `org_enforce_todo_dependencies` or `org_enforce_todo_checkbox_dependencies`); `invisible` leaves them out instead, except those blocked by checkboxes, which stay dimmed. (`org-agenda-dim-blocked-tasks`)

org_enforce_todo_checkbox_dependencies.description: An entry cannot be done while it has an unchecked box. (`org-enforce-todo-checkbox-dependencies`)

org_log_refile.description: Record when an entry is refiled (`Refiled on [2026-05-18 Mon 10:30]`), with `note` asking for a note too. `#+STARTUP:` `logrefile`, `lognoterefile` and `nologrefile` change it in the file refiled to. (`org-log-refile`)

org_log_reschedule.description: Record when a scheduled date changes or is removed (`Rescheduled from "[2026-05-18 Mon]" on …`), with `note` asking for a note too. `#+STARTUP:` `logreschedule`, `lognotereschedule` and `nologreschedule` change it in a file. (`org-log-reschedule`)

org_log_redeadline.description: Record when a deadline changes or is removed (`New deadline from …`), with `note` asking for a note too. `#+STARTUP:` `logredeadline`, `lognoteredeadline` and `nologredeadline` change it in a file. (`org-log-redeadline`)

org_log_into_drawer.description: Put state changes and notes into a drawer: `true` for `LOGBOOK`, or the name of a drawer. `#+STARTUP:` `logdrawer` and `nologdrawer` change it in a file; an entry's `LOG_INTO_DRAWER` property (inherited) says which drawer for it (`t` for `LOGBOOK`, `nil` for none). (`org-log-into-drawer`)

org_log_done_with_time.description: The `CLOSED:` timestamp of an entry done has the time, not only the date. (`org-log-done-with-time`)

org_log_note_headings.description: The heading of each kind of note, by kind: `done` (`CLOSING NOTE %t`), `state` (`State %-12s from %-12S %t`), `note`, `reschedule`, `delschedule`, `redeadline`, `deldeadline`, `refile` and `clock_out`. In a heading `%t` is the time, `%T` the time active, `%d` and `%D` the date, `%s` the new state or date and `%S` the old one, `%u` the login name and `%U` the full name; an empty heading leaves the note its text only. Kinds left out keep Org's headings. Habits take notes with the `done` heading for days done. (`org-log-note-headings`)

org_log_states_order_reversed.description: Put a new state note, note or clock line above the others (`false`: below them). `#+STARTUP:` `logstatesreversed` and `nologstatesreversed` change it in a file. (`org-log-states-order-reversed`)

org_log_state_notes_insert_after_drawers.description: Without a log drawer, put notes after the drawers right under the headline and planning line, not before them. (`org-log-state-notes-insert-after-drawers`)

org_log_note_clock_out.description: Ask for a note when the clock stops (`org.clock.out`), which goes right after the clock line. `#+STARTUP:` `lognoteclock-out` and `nolognoteclock-out` change it in a file. (`org-log-note-clock-out`)

org_provide_todo_statistics.description: Update the `[1/3]` and `[33%]` cookies of the parent when a state changes, counting the entries with a keyword (`true`), every entry (`all-headlines`, those without a keyword as not done), those with these keywords and the done ones (a list), or those of the first list as not done and of the second as done (two lists). `false` leaves the cookies. (`org-provide-todo-statistics`)

org_hierarchical_todo_statistics.description: TODO statistics count the children only; `false`: the whole subtree, and the cookies above too. A `COOKIE_DATA` property with `recursive` does this for a subtree. (`org-hierarchical-todo-statistics`)

org_closed_keep_when_no_todo.description: Keep the `CLOSED:` timestamp when an entry is left with no keyword. (`org-closed-keep-when-no-todo`)

org_todo_state_tags_triggers.description: Tags that change with the state, by state: a keyword, `""` for none, `todo` for any not done, `done` for any done; each a list of tags to set (`+TAG`) or remove (`-TAG`), in order: `{ "WAIT": ["+waiting"], "todo": ["-done"], "done": ["+done", "-waiting"] }`. (`org-todo-state-tags-triggers`)

org_tags_column.description: Where tags are aligned after a change to a headline. Negative: they end at that column. (`org-tags-column`)

org_use_tag_inheritance.description: Which tags entries inherit from their parents and from `#+FILETAGS:`: `true` for all, `false` for none, a list of tags, or a regexp (Emacs syntax) tags must match. Inherited tags count in tag searches and show in the agenda. (`org-use-tag-inheritance`)

org_tags_exclude_from_inheritance.description: Tags never inherited, when `org_use_tag_inheritance` is `true` or a regexp. (`org-tags-exclude-from-inheritance`)

org_use_property_inheritance.description: Which properties an entry without them takes from its parents, the file's property drawer and `#+PROPERTY:` lines, in property searches (`OWNER="alice"`): `true` for all, `false` for none, a list of names, or a regexp (Emacs syntax). `CATEGORY` and `ARCHIVE` are always inherited. (`org-use-property-inheritance`)

org_property_separators.description: What joins the values of a property with those of its `PROPERTY+` lines, and the inherited ones, instead of a space: `[["AUTHOR", "COAUTHOR"], ", "]` for the properties named, `["^TAG", ";"]` for those an Emacs regexp matches, without regard to case. The first that fits counts. (`org-property-separators`)

org_property_format.description: How a property line is written when it is indented (TAB, `org.indent`) or set: `format`'s `%s` for the key with its colons, then the value, with a width (`%-10s` pads the key to 10 columns). (`org-property-format`)

org_global_properties.description: Properties every entry inherits, after those of `#+PROPERTY:` lines: chiefly the allowed values of a property, which setting it offers and `S-<right>` and `S-<left>` go through on its line (`{ "Effort_ALL": "0:10 0:30 1:00 2:00" }`; `:ETC` allows others too). (`org-global-properties`)

org_clock_into_drawer.description: Where `CLOCK:` lines go: `true` for the drawer of `org_log_into_drawer` (`LOGBOOK` when that is not a name), the name of a drawer, or `false` for the entry itself. (`org-clock-into-drawer`)

org_clock_out_remove_zero_time_clocks.description: Clocking out after less than a minute removes the `CLOCK:` line. (`org-clock-out-remove-zero-time-clocks`)

org_clock_out_when_done.description: Marking the clocked entry done stops the clock. (`org-clock-out-when-done`)

org_clock_display_default_range.description: The span whose clocks `org.clock.display` (`C-c C-x C-d`) adds up. (`org-clock-display-default-range`)

org_clock_idle_time.description: After how many minutes without a message from the editor a clock that runs asks what to do with the idle time: keep it, subtract it (and clock out), or cancel the clock. (`org-clock-idle-time`)

org_clock_auto_clock_resolution.description: Clocking in first asks about each clock left running in the open and agenda files, as `org.clock.resolve` does: `when-no-clock-is-running` when no clock runs, `true` always (the clock that runs too), `false` never. A clock found running when the server starts, or written by hand, is no clock the server ran: it is asked about. (`org-clock-auto-clock-resolution`)

org_clock_resolve_expert.description: Ask what to do with a dangling clock or idle time with the keys in the prompt alone (`[jkKtTgGSscCiq]?`), without the list of what each one does. (`org-clock-resolve-expert`)

org_clock_history_length.description: How many entries clocked into the clock history keeps, for `org.clock.in` with a count and `org.clock.in.last`. (`org-clock-history-length`)

org_clock_in_resume.description: Clocking into an entry whose `CLOCK:` line was left without an end goes on with that clock, from when it started, rather than starting a new line. (`org-clock-in-resume`)

org_clock_persist.description: Keep the running clock and the clock history when the server stops, and take them back when it starts: `true` both, `clock` the running clock alone, `history` the history alone (what `C-u C-c C-x C-i` offers). The running clock runs again if its `CLOCK:` line is still open. They are kept in Emacs's own file, in its form, so Emacs and org-lsp take the clock from each other. (`org-clock-persist`)

org_clock_persist_file.description: The file `org_clock_persist` keeps the clock in: Emacs's, `org-clock-save.el` in its directory. (`org-clock-persist-file`)

org_clock_persist_query_resume.description: Ask before the clock the last session kept runs again (`Resume clock (…)?`). (`org-clock-persist-query-resume`)

org_clock_goto_may_find_recent_task.description: With no clock running, `org.clock.goto` goes to the entry clocked last. With `false`, it says `No active or recent clock task`. (`org-clock-goto-may-find-recent-task`)

org_clock_clocktable_default_properties.description: The parameters a new clock table gets on its `#+BEGIN:` line from `org.clock.report` (`C-c C-x C-r`), after `:scope`, as Emacs Lisp reads them (`:maxlevel 3 :link t`). (`org-clock-clocktable-default-properties`)

org_clocktable_defaults.description: The parameters every clock table has unless its `#+BEGIN:` line gives them, as Emacs Lisp reads them. Set, it replaces Org's whole list. (`org-clocktable-defaults`)

org_clock_clocktable_language_setup.description: The words of a clock table in each language its `:lang` names: the language, then its words for `File`, `L`, `Timestamp`, `Headline`, `Time`, `ALL`, `Total time`, `File time` and `Clock summary at`. A word left out stays English. Set, it replaces Org's languages. (`org-clock-clocktable-language-setup`)

org_clock_report_include_clocking_task.description: A clock table counts the time of the clock that runs, for its entry, when the table covers a time (`:block`, `:tstart` and `:tend`) and the clock started within it. (`org-clock-report-include-clocking-task`)

org_clock_rounding_minutes.description: Clocking in and out happens at the multiple of this many minutes nearest now; a clock never starts later than now. Below 1, at the minute. (`org-clock-rounding-minutes`)

org_clock_continuously.description: A clock starts when the last one stopped, not now. (`org-clock-continuously`)

org_clock_total_time_cell_format.description: How a clock table writes its total time and the words before it; `%s` is the text. (`org-clock-total-time-cell-format`)

org_clock_file_time_cell_format.description: How a clock table over several files writes the words before a file's time; `%s` is the text. (`org-clock-file-time-cell-format`)

org_clock_in_switch_to_state.description: The TODO state an entry is put in when the clock starts on it (`NEXT`), unless it has it already. (`org-clock-in-switch-to-state`)

org_clock_out_switch_to_state.description: The TODO state an entry is put in when the clock stops on it. (`org-clock-out-switch-to-state`)

org_lint.description: Org's linter checks the documents and reports what it finds as diagnostics: misplaced headings and planning lines, links to nowhere, duplicate names, footnotes without definitions… What it finds is information, a hint for a checker Org trusts little: an Org file is text, nothing in it is an error or a warning. (`org-lint`)

org_lint_ignore.description: The `org-lint` checkers to leave out, by name, as a diagnostic's code shows it (`"misplaced-heading"`). (`org-lint`)

org_id_method.description: How a new `ID` is made (`org.id.create`, a link stored by ID, org-roam): a random UUID, the time in base 36 (`org`), or the time as `org_id_ts_format` writes it (`ts`). (`org-id-method`)

org_id_prefix.description: What a new `ID` starts with, before a colon: `"Org"` makes `Org:…`. (`org-id-prefix`)

org_id_ts_format.description: How the `ts` method writes the time, as `format-time-string` does. (`org-id-ts-format`)

org_id_include_domain.description: The `org` and `ts` methods end a new `ID` with `@` and the machine's domain. (`org-id-include-domain`)

org_id_track_globally.description: IDs are looked for in other files than the link's own: those of `org_id_search_archives`, `org_id_extra_files` and `org_id_locations_file`, the agenda files, the open ones and org-roam's. Off, an `id:` link leads only within its file. (`org-id-track-globally`)

org_id_search_archives.description: IDs are looked for in the archive files of the agenda files too. (`org-id-search-archives`)

org_id_extra_files.description: More files to look for IDs in: paths or glob patterns. (`org-id-extra-files`)

org_id_locations_file.description: The file where Emacs keeps the files it found IDs in: org-lsp looks in them too, and never writes it. Names in it that are not absolute are relative to its directory. (`org-id-locations-file`)

files.description: `current` (the entry's own file), `agenda`, `org-id-files` (the files with IDs), a path or a list of paths

maxlevel.description: The headlines up to this level

todo.description: The headlines with this TODO keyword

regexp.description: The headlines that match this regular expression

org_id_completion_targets.description: The headlines an `id:` link completes to (`org.link.insert`), as `org_refile_targets` names them: by default every headline of the file and of the files with IDs. (`org-id-completion-targets`)

org_link_search_must_match_exact_headlin.description: What a link to a headline that is not there does: `"query-to-create"` asks whether to make it, at the end of the file, when the link is followed (`org.open`); `true` is an error; `false` looks for its words in the text. (`org-link-search-must-match-exact-headline`)

org_link_doi_server_url.description: What a `doi:` link is opened at: this, then the DOI. (`org-link-doi-server-url`)

org_link_shell_skip_confirm_regexp.description: An Emacs regexp: a `shell:` link whose command it matches runs when followed without asking `Execute … in shell?` first. Empty asks for every command. (`org-link-shell-skip-confirm-regexp`)

org_man_command.description: The program that writes the man page of a `man:` link, when `ol-man` is in `org_modules`: the page is shown as text, at the line before the first match of what follows `::` (`man:ls::-l`). `"woman"`, Emacs's own reader, is `man` too. (`org-man-command`)

org_info_other_documents.description: The pages on the web of Info manuals: following an `info:` link to one of them, or to one of Emacs's manuals, opens its page at the node. Another manual is shown as text, as the `info` program writes the node. (`org-info-other-documents`)

org_ctags_path_to_ctags.description: The `ctags` program (Exuberant or Universal Ctags) that `org.ctags.create` runs to make the `TAGS` file of a directory, when `org-ctags` is in `org_modules`. (`org-ctags-path-to-ctags`)

org_ctags_open_link_functions.description: With `org-ctags` in `org_modules`, what following a link to a headline, a target or a custom ID tries first, in turn, until one is done: `org-ctags-find-tag` (the tag of the `TAGS` file of the file's directory), `org-ctags-ask-rebuild-tags-file-then-find-tag` and `org-ctags-rebuild-tags-file-then-find-tag` (the `TAGS` file made again, then the tag), `org-ctags-ask-append-topic` and `org-ctags-append-topic` (a new topic at the end of the file), `org-ctags-ask-visit-buffer-or-file` and `org-ctags-visit-buffer-or-file` (the Org file of that name in the directory, made when asked), `org-ctags-fail-silently` (nothing more). When none is done, the link is followed as without them. (`org-ctags-open-link-functions`)

org_ctags_new_topic_template.description: The text of a new topic `org_ctags_open_link_functions` makes, `%t` the link's text capitalized. (`org-ctags-new-topic-template`)

org_id_link_to_org_use_id.description: Whether `org.link.store` (`C-c l`) links to an entry by its ID: `true` makes one when the entry has none, `"create-if-interactive"` only from the command (not for capture's `%a`), `"create-if-interactive-and-no-custom-id"` likewise unless the entry has a `CUSTOM_ID`, `"use-existing"` only when it has one already. Off, the link searches for the headline. (`org-id-link-to-org-use-id`)

org_link_context_for_files.description: Links to a place in a file search for it (`file:notes.org::*Heading`); `C-u` turns it around for one link. (`org-link-context-for-files`)

org_id_link_use_context.description: ID links to a place below the entry's headline search for it as well (`id:…::name`). (`org-id-link-use-context`)

org_id_link_consider_parent_id.description: An ID link may use the ID of a parent entry, with a search for the place. (`org-id-link-consider-parent-id`)

org_link_file_path_type.description: How links to files write the path: `"adaptive"` relative below the file's directory and absolute elsewhere, `"absolute"` (with `~`), `"noabbrev"` (without), `"relative"`. (`org-link-file-path-type`)

org_link_keep_stored_after_insertion.description: Stored links stay stored once inserted. (`org-link-keep-stored-after-insertion`)

org_complete_tags_always_offer_all_agend.description: Completing a tag offers the tags of every agenda file, after those of the file. Off, only the file's own. Setting tags offers them too. (`org-complete-tags-always-offer-all-agenda-tags`)

org_cite_global_bibliography.description: Bibliography files for the citations of every document (`[cite:@key]`), after those its `#+BIBLIOGRAPHY:` lines name: BibTeX (`.bib`, `.bibtex`) or CSL-JSON (`.json`). Their entries are completed after `@`, shown over a key, and where following a key goes; a key none has is marked. (`org-cite-global-bibliography`)

org_cite_insert_processor.description: The citation processor `org.cite.insert` inserts with: `basic`, as Org's own does; Org's other processors cannot insert, and those of packages (citar) are not run; `false` for none. (`org-cite-insert-processor`)

org_bibtex_autogen_keys.description: Whether `org.bibtex.create` and `org.bibtex.check` make the key of a new BibTeX entry from its author, year and title, as `bibtex-generate-autokey` makes it (through Emacs), instead of asking for it (`id`). (`org-bibtex-autogen-keys`)

org_bibtex_prefix.description: What the names of the properties the BibTeX commands write start with (`BIB_` gives `BIB_AUTHOR`), but for the key's; they read the names with it and without. (`org-bibtex-prefix`)

org_bibtex_treat_headline_as_title.description: A headline without a `TITLE` property is the title of its BibTeX entry, and `org.bibtex.check` does not ask for one. (`org-bibtex-treat-headline-as-title`)

org_bibtex_export_arbitrary_fields.description: With `org_bibtex_prefix`, every property whose name has the prefix is a field of the entry exported (`org.bibtex.export`, `org.bibtex.copy`), not only those of its type. (`org-bibtex-export-arbitrary-fields`)

org_bibtex_key_property.description: The property that holds an entry's BibTeX key. `ID` makes the key a global ID. (`org-bibtex-key-property`)

org_bibtex_tags.description: Tags given to the entries the BibTeX commands make. (`org-bibtex-tags`)

org_bibtex_tags_are_keywords.description: The `keywords` field of an entry read is its tags (spaces as `_`, other characters a tag cannot have left out), and an entry's own tags are its `keywords` when exported, but for those of `org_bibtex_tags` and `org_bibtex_no_export_tags`. (`org-bibtex-tags-are-keywords`)

org_bibtex_no_export_tags.description: Tags that are not exported as keywords, with `org_bibtex_tags_are_keywords`. (`org-bibtex-no-export-tags`)

org_bibtex_inherit_tags.description: With `org_bibtex_tags_are_keywords`, the tags an entry inherits are keywords too. (`org-bibtex-inherit-tags`)

org_bibtex_type_property_name.description: The property that holds an entry's BibTeX type (`article`); a headline without it is no entry. (`org-bibtex-type-property-name`)

org_link_abbrev_alist.description: Link abbreviations: `[[gh:org-lsp]]` with `{ "gh": "https://github.com/%s" }` follows `https://github.com/org-lsp`. `%s` stands for what follows the colon, `%h` for it URL-encoded; without either it goes at the end. A file's `#+LINK:` lines come first. `%(my-function)` calls an Emacs function with what follows the colon (through Emacs). (`org-link-abbrev-alist`)

org_file_apps.description: What opens a linked file, the first entry that matches: a match is an extension (`txt`), an Emacs regular expression for the file name (`\\.pdf\\'` in JSON; with groups `%1`, `%2`... in the command, it matches the file followed by the link's `::` part), `directory`, `remote`, `system` (what `C-u C-u C-c C-o` uses), `auto-mode` (every file the editor can show) or `t` (any other file). A command is `emacs` (the editor), `default` (the `system` entry, else the editor), `system` or `mailcap` (the system's application, through the editor), or a shell command where `%s` is the file. `C-u C-c C-o` opens the file in the editor. A Lisp function is not a command here. (`org-file-apps`)

org_open_non_existing_files.description: Open a linked file that is not there with the application `org_file_apps` gives it, rather than saying `No such file`. The editor opens such a file either way. (`org-open-non-existing-files`)

org_open_directory_means_index_dot_org.description: Following a link to a directory opens the `index.org` in it, rather than the directory. (`org-open-directory-means-index-dot-org`)

org_tag_alist.description: The tags offered when setting tags in a file without a `#+TAGS:` line, written like one: `"work(w) home(h) { @office(o) @home(m) } [ GTD : Control Persp ]"` gives `work` the key `w`, makes `@office` and `@home` exclusive, and groups `Control` and `Persp` under `GTD`; `\n` starts a new line. A list of these words does as well. Unset, the tags used in the file are offered. (`org-tag-alist`)

org_tag_persistent_alist.description: Tags offered in every file, before those of `#+TAGS:` or `org_tag_alist`, written the same way. (`org-tag-persistent-alist`)

org_group_tags.description: A group tag (`[ GTD : Control Persp ]`, `{ Context : @home @office }` in `#+TAGS:` or `org_tag_alist`) in the match string of a tags view stands for itself and the tags of its group. (`org-group-tags`)

org_use_fast_todo_selection.description: How `C-c C-t` (`org.todo`) changes the TODO state where keywords have keys (`TODO(t)`): `auto` picks the state by key from a menu of them; `expert` by key too, the keys listed in the prompt alone (in Neovim and Vim; other editors show their menu); `false` goes to the next state, as where no keyword has a key. `true` is `auto`. (`org-use-fast-todo-selection`)

org_use_fast_tag_selection.description: Pick tags by key, each key turning its tag on or off until RET: `auto` when some tag has a key, `true` always (keys are given to the tags without one), `false` never: the tags are typed instead. (`org-use-fast-tag-selection`)

org_fast_tag_selection_single_key.description: In fast tag selection, the first key that changes the tags also ends it. (`org-fast-tag-selection-single-key`)

org_tags_sort_function.description: Sort the tags of a headline when they are set: alphabetically, or the other way. (`org-tags-sort-function`)

org_auto_align_tags.description: Align the tags of a headline to `org_tags_column` when they are set. (`org-auto-align-tags`)

org_todo_repeat_to_state.description: The state a repeating entry returns to when it is done: a keyword, or `true` for the state it had. (`org-todo-repeat-to-state`)

org_priority_default.description: The priority of an entry without a cookie. A file's `#+PRIORITIES:` line takes precedence over the three priority options. (`org-priority-default`)

org_priority_start_cycle_with_default.description: Raising or lowering the priority of an entry that has none starts at the default. (`org-priority-start-cycle-with-default`)

org_time_stamp_rounding_minutes.description: The step in which the minutes of a timestamp change (the second number of Org's option). (`org-time-stamp-rounding-minutes`)

org_read_date_prefer_future.description: A date typed without a year or month is the next one to come. With `time`, a time that has passed today is tomorrow's. (`org-read-date-prefer-future`)

org_agenda_jump_prefer_future.description: How the agenda's `j` (`org.agenda.goto.date`) reads a date typed without a year or month, as `org_read_date_prefer_future` does for every other prompt. (`org-agenda-jump-prefer-future`)

org_read_date_force_compatible_dates.description: A typed year is kept within 1970 to 2037. (`org-read-date-force-compatible-dates`)

files.description: `current` (the entry's own file), `agenda`, `org-id-files` (the files with IDs), a path or a list of paths

maxlevel.description: The headlines up to this level

todo.description: The headlines with this TODO keyword

regexp.description: The headlines that match this regular expression

org_refile_targets.description: Where entries can be refiled to. Each entry has `files`: `current` (the entry's own file), `agenda`, `org-id-files` (the files with IDs), a path or a list of paths; and one of `level`, `maxlevel`, `tag`, `todo`, `regexp` (the Rust `regex` crate's syntax) or `all` (true), which says which headlines there are targets. (`org-refile-targets`)

org_refile_use_outline_path.description: Name targets by their outline path (`Projects/Alpha/`). The three names start the path with the file, and offer the file itself, for its top level. (`org-refile-use-outline-path`)

org_refile_active_region_within_subtree.description: A selection that is not whole subtrees is refiled too: its first line becomes a headline first (`org-toggle-heading`, run by Emacs), a level below the entry it is in. (`org-refile-active-region-within-subtree`)

org_refile_allow_creating_parent_nodes.description: A target that is not there yet can be named after an existing one, `Projects/New`: it is made, as the last child of `Projects`, and the entry goes under it. `confirm` asks first. (`org-refile-allow-creating-parent-nodes`)

org_refile_target_verify_function.description: The name of an Emacs Lisp function that decides which headlines are refile targets: the server's Emacs calls it at the start of each, and keeps those it says yes to. Where it leaves the point, the search goes on: a function can skip a subtree. (`org-refile-target-verify-function`)

org_reverse_note_order.description: A refiled entry goes first under its target, not last. (`org-reverse-note-order`)

org_archive_location.description: Where archived subtrees go: a file, `::`, and a headline under which they go (they go to the end of the file without one). `%s` is the name of the file the subtree is in; an empty file part is that file. `datetree/` as the headline files them under year, month and day, by when they were closed. An `ARCHIVE` property of the entry or a parent, or a `#+ARCHIVE:` line, says otherwise. (`org-archive-location`)

org_archive_reversed_order.description: An archived subtree goes first under its archive headline, not last. (`org-archive-reversed-order`)

org_archive_mark_done.description: Mark archived entries done: `true` for the first done keyword, or the keyword to use. (`org-archive-mark-done`)

org_archive_subtree_add_inherited_tags.description: Give an archived subtree the tags it inherited: always, never, or when it stays in its file. (`org-archive-subtree-add-inherited-tags`)

org_archive_save_context_info.description: What an archived entry keeps as `ARCHIVE_…` properties: `time`, `file`, `olpath` (its outline path), `category`, `todo`, `itags` (inherited tags), `ltags` (its own tags) and `olid` (its parent's ID). (`org-archive-save-context-info`)

org_archive_sibling_heading.description: The headline of the sibling `org.archive.sibling` archives under. (`org-archive-sibling-heading`)

org_archive_file_header_format.description: What a new archive file starts with; `%s` is the path of the file the subtree came from. (`org-archive-file-header-format`)

org_archive_default_command.description: What `org.archive.default` does: archive the subtree, archive it under its sibling, or tag it. (`org-archive-default-command`)

org_archive_subtree_save_file_p.description: Whether the archive file is saved once a subtree goes there: always (`true`), when archiving from an Org file (`from-org`), from the agenda (`from-agenda`), or never (`false`). Unsaved, it is left with its changes in the editor, as `auto_save` does not save it. (`org-archive-subtree-save-file-p`)

org_capture_use_agenda_date.description: Capturing from the agenda takes the day of the line the cursor is on, at midnight (or the hour of `org_extend_today_until`), for `%t`, `%U` and the like and for the date of a date tree, which a `time_prompt` template then does not ask for. (`org-capture-use-agenda-date`)

key.description: The keys the context is about

use.description: The keys whose template or command these keys stand for where the context holds

contexts.description: Rules, each a regexp on the file, the mode or the buffer's name; the context holds where one of them does

org_capture_templates_contexts.description: Where templates are offered. Each has the `key` of a template, `contexts`, rules such as `{ "in_file": "work" }` (`in_file`, `in_mode`, `in_buffer`, `not_in_file`, `not_in_mode` or `not_in_buffer`, each with a regexp of the `regex` crate's syntax, matched ignoring case), and maybe `use`, the key of the template it stands for there. A template with contexts is offered only where one of their rules holds. The mode is `org-mode` in an Org file and `org-agenda-mode` in the agenda, where there is no file; the buffer's name is the file's. (`org-capture-templates-contexts`)

key.description: The keys that pick the template

type.description: An Org entry (the default), plain text, a list item, a checkbox item or a table line

target.description: `file` and a path; `file+headline`, a path and a headline; `file+olp`, a path and the headlines of an outline path; `file+regexp`, a path and a regular expression; `file+olp+datetree`, a path and maybe an outline path; `id` and an ID; `clock`; `file+function`, a path and an Emacs Lisp function; or `function` and an Emacs Lisp function that visits the file

prepend.description: First under the target, not last

tree_type.description: The levels of a date tree

time_prompt.description: Ask for the date of the date tree entry

table_line_pos.description: Where a table line goes: `II-1` is above the second rule

clock_in.description: Clock the captured entry while the capture goes on

clock_keep.description: Keep the clock running when the capture is filed

clock_resume.description: Start the clock the capture stopped again

jump_to_captured.description: Show the captured entry in its file

unnarrowed.description: Show the whole target file in the capture buffer

org_capture_templates.description: Capture templates. Each has a `key`, a `description`, a `type` (`entry`, the default, `plain`, `item`, `checkitem` or `table-line`), a `target` and a `template` (text, or a list of lines), and may have `prepend`, `empty_lines`, `empty_lines_before`, `empty_lines_after`, `immediate_finish`, `tree_type`, `time_prompt`, `table_line_pos`, `clock_in`, `clock_keep`, `clock_resume`, `jump_to_captured` and `unnarrowed`. The target is a list: `file` and a path; `file+headline`, a path and a headline; `file+olp`, a path and the headlines of an outline path; `file+regexp`, a path and a regular expression; `file+olp+datetree`, a path and the headlines of an outline path, maybe none, for a date tree under them; `id` and an ID; `clock`, the entry clocked now; `file+function`, a path and the name of an Emacs Lisp function that moves the point there, or `function` and the name of one that visits the file too (run by the server's Emacs). An empty path is `org_default_notes_file`, and without a target the entry goes at the end of `org_default_notes_file`. A template with only a key and a description groups the templates whose keys start with its key. (`org-capture-templates`)

org_protocol_default_template_key.description: The keys of the capture template an `org-protocol://capture` URL uses when it names none (`template=`). (`org-protocol-default-template-key`)

org_protocol_data_separator.description: An Emacs regular expression: what separates the parts of an old-style `org-protocol` URL (`org-protocol://capture:/x/URL/TITLE/BODY`). (`org-protocol-data-separator`)

base_url.description: The URL of the published pages, with its last slash

working_directory.description: The directory of their files, with its last slash

rewrites.description: Pairs of an Emacs regexp on the URL and a path, for URLs whose file is not there

org_protocol_project_alist.description: Where the files of `org-protocol://open-source` URLs are on this computer. Each has a `name`, the `base_url` of the pages (with its last slash) and the `working_directory` of their files (with its last slash, `~/` for the home directory), and may have an `online_suffix` taken off the URL (`.html`), a `working_suffix` put on in its place (`.org`), and `rewrites`, pairs of an Emacs regular expression on the URL, whose first group is taken out of it, and what goes after it, for a URL whose file is not there. The first whose `base_url` the URL has is tried first. (`org-protocol-project-alist`)

org_protocol_editor.description: The editor `org-lsp protocol` starts when no org-lsp runs, as a command line (`code`, `zed`, `kitty nvim`): it opens `org_default_notes_file` in it, or the file of an `open-source` URL, and the org-lsp that starts there takes the URL, within two minutes. Read from the shared file only. Without it, a stored link is kept for the next org-lsp that starts, and a capture fails.

org_directory.description: Where the relative paths of capture targets are. (`org-directory`)

org_default_notes_file.description: The target of a capture template whose file is empty. (`org-default-notes-file`)

org_link_descriptive.description: Show a link as its description (or its target, when it has none) and hide the rest: the brackets, and the target of a link with a description. The text is marked `hidden` in the highlighting, and editors that can conceal text conceal it. (`org-link-descriptive`)

org_hide_emphasis_markers.description: Hide the markers around `*bold*`, `/italic/`, `_underline_`, `+strike-through+`, `=verbatim=` and `~code~`, as for links. (`org-hide-emphasis-markers`)

org_fontify_emphasized_text.description: Show `*bold*`, `/italic/`, `_underline_`, `+strike-through+`, `=verbatim=` and `~code~` in their looks. With `false` they look as the text around them, their markers shown. (`org-fontify-emphasized-text`)

org_emphasis_alist.description: The look of each kind of emphasis, by its marker (`*`, `/`, `_`, `=`, `~`, `+`): a face of Org's, `bold`, `italic`, `bold-italic`, `underline`, `org-code` or `org-verbatim`, attributes as Org writes them (`:weight bold :slant italic :underline t :strike-through t`), or a list of them; `false` for none. As in Emacs, a marker left out has no look. Colors are not shown. (`org-emphasis-alist`)

org_hidden_keywords.description: The keywords hidden before their values, such as `#+TITLE:` with `["title"]`, in editors that conceal text. (`org-hidden-keywords`)

org_hide_macro_markers.description: Hide the braces of macro calls, `{{{` and `}}}`, in editors that conceal text. (`org-hide-macro-markers`)

org_display_custom_times.description: Show timestamps in `org_timestamp_custom_formats`: the date and time inside the brackets is hidden and the custom form shows in its place, as entities do. `#+STARTUP: customtime` turns it on for a file, and `C-c C-x C-t` (`org.timestamp.overlays.toggle`) on and off. Exports through Emacs use them too; the date prompt shows its answer in Org's own form. (`org-display-custom-times`)

org_timestamp_custom_formats.description: The formats of `org_display_custom_times`, as `format-time-string` reads them (`%d.%m.%Y`); brackets around a format are dropped. (`org-timestamp-custom-formats`)

org_entities_user.description: Entities of your own, used as `\name`: what each is in LaTeX (and whether that needs math mode), HTML, ASCII, Latin-1 and UTF-8, as `["myarrow", "\\to", true, "→", "->", "->", "→"]`. A name is letters only, and one of Org's own is replaced. The server shows them as `org_pretty_entities` says and completes them; Emacs exports them. (`org-entities-user`)

org_pretty_entities.description: Show entities (`\alpha`, `\to`) as their character (`α`, `→`): the entity is hidden as link brackets are, and its character is an inlay hint in its place. (`org-pretty-entities`)

org_pretty_entities_include_sub_superscr.description: With `org_pretty_entities`, show sub- and superscripts (`x^2`, `H_{2}O`, `a_{n}`) raised and lowered: in Unicode (`x²`, `H₂O`, `aₙ`) where every character has a raised or lowered form, as an inlay hint in place of the hidden text; the others are left as they are. (`org-pretty-entities-include-sub-superscripts`)

org_use_sub_superscripts.description: Which sub- and superscripts `org_pretty_entities` shows: all, only those in braces (`a_{b}`, `"{}"`), or none. (`org-use-sub-superscripts`)

return_uses_meta_return.description: RET on the first line of a list item makes the next item, numbered and with a checkbox as M-RET (`org-meta-return`) makes it, the items after it renumbered, as nvim-orgmode's `org_return_uses_meta_return` does. Off, RET is Org's: a new line in the item. `org.return.item` (`<S-CR>`, Shift+Enter, with the vim keys) always does it.

org_return_follows_link.description: RET (`org.return`) on a link, a timestamp or a citation follows it, as `org.open` (`C-c C-o`) does. In a table RET still moves down. (`org-return-follows-link`)

calendar_months.description: How many months the calendar of the date prompt shows: 3 side by side, as Emacs's calendar shows them, the one with the selected day in the middle; or 1, that month alone, for a narrow window, with the answer on a line under the prompt.

calendar_week_start_day.description: The day the weeks of the date prompt's calendar start on: 1 starts them on Monday. (`calendar-week-start-day`)

emacs.description: The Emacs program, for what only Org itself does: export (`org.export.dispatch`). The server starts it (`emacs --batch -Q`) when that is first asked for and keeps it running, so that Org loads once. Without Emacs, everything else works as before.

emacs_config_file.description: A file of Emacs Lisp that Emacs loads before Org, for the variables export reads (`org-export-backends`, `org-html-…`, `org-latex-…`, `org-publish-project-alist`): a file of its own, or your init file. `~/` is the home directory.

emacs_config.description: Emacs Lisp that Emacs evaluates after `emacs_config_file` and before loading Org, for a few settings without a file that `emacs_options` cannot say: a function or a hook, or `(add-to-list 'load-path "~/src/org-mode/lisp")` for another Org. A yes-or-no question Emacs asks while it works (`org-confirm-babel-evaluate`) is asked in the editor.

     function CodeHighlightOn(elem, id)

emacs_options.description: Org's options for what Emacs does, by their names in Org, which Emacs sets as Customize does: `{ "org-attach-method": "mv", "org-export-with-toc": false }`. `true` is `t` and `false` `nil`, a list is a list and a table an association list; a string is a symbol where the option takes one. Each is set when Emacs loads the library it is in, after `emacs_config_file` and `emacs_config`, and so wins over them. A value the option does not take is left out, with a message. The options, each with Org's documentation of it, are in `docs/emacs-options.org`; the others are settings of the server, or Lisp (functions, hooks), which goes in `emacs_config`.

auto_save.description: Save the files a command changes other than the one it was run in: an entry's file changed from the agenda, the target of a capture or of a refile. The editor saves them once it has made the change. Off, they are left with unsaved changes, as Emacs leaves them.
