org_cycle_max_level.description: The deepest headlines that fold; deeper ones are text of the subtree they are in. (`org-cycle-max-level`)

org_cycle_global_at_bob.description: TAB at the very start of the file, when its first line is no headline, cycles the whole file as S-TAB does. (`org-cycle-global-at-bob`)

org_cycle_level_after_item_entry_creatio.description: TAB on a new, empty headline makes it a child of the headline before, then each level up, then a sibling again; on an empty item, it indents and outdents the item the same way. (`org-cycle-level-after-item/entry-creation`)

org_startup_folded.description: How files show when opened: `"overview"` (or `"fold"`) only the top headlines, `"content"` all the headlines, `"show2levels"` to `"show5levels"` the headlines down to that level, `"showeverything"` (or `"nofold"`, `"showall"`) everything. `#+STARTUP:` decides for a file. Unless everything shows, a subtree's `VISIBILITY` property (`folded`, `children`, `content`, `all`) decides for it, archived subtrees are folded, and drawers too. Folds hide whole subtrees, so where Org shows a headline's children but not its text, the text shows. (`org-startup-folded`)

org_startup_align_all_tables.description: Align every table of a file when it opens (an edit of the file, as in Emacs). `#+STARTUP: align` and `noalign` decide for a file. (`org-startup-align-all-tables`)

org_startup_shrink_all_tables.description: Shrink the columns of every table that have a width cookie (`<10>`) when a file opens. `#+STARTUP: shrink` decides for a file. Shrunk fields show their first characters and `…`, in editors that can hide text. (`org-startup-shrink-all-tables`)

org_cycle_hide_block_startup.description: Fold blocks when a file opens folded (`org_startup_folded`). `#+STARTUP: hideblocks` and `nohideblocks` decide for a file. (`org-cycle-hide-block-startup`)

org_cycle_hide_drawer_startup.description: Fold drawers when a file opens folded (`org_startup_folded`). (`org-cycle-hide-drawer-startup`)

org_cycle_open_archived_trees.description: Leave archived subtrees open when a file opens folded (`org_startup_folded`). (`org-cycle-open-archived-trees`)

org_adapt_indentation.description: Indent the lines of an entry past its headline's stars: `true` for all of them, `"headline-data"` for the planning line, drawers and clock lines right below the headline. Applies to new lines, to re-indenting (range formatting) and to what commands write. (`org-adapt-indentation`)

org_image_actual_width.description: How wide the image of a link shows: `true` at its own width; a number, that many pixels; `false` or a list of one number, the `:width` of the paragraph's `#+ATTR_ORG:` or else of another `#+ATTR_…:` (pixels, `50%` or a fraction up to 2 of the text's width, `t` for its own width), else the list's number. An entry's `ORG-IMAGE-ACTUAL-WIDTH` property decides for its own text. (`org-image-actual-width`)

org_image_max_width.description: How wide at most an image shown at its own width is: `"fill-column"`, 70 columns; `"window"`, the window's width; an integer, that many pixels; a float, that part of the window's width; null for no limit. (`org-image-max-width`)

org_display_remote_inline_images.description: Whether the images of `http:` and `https:` links show (`C-c C-x C-v`): `"skip"` not; `"download"` downloaded each time they show; `"cache"` downloaded once and kept for the session. The download follows `org_resource_download_policy`; an image larger than 20 MB is not downloaded. (`org-display-remote-inline-images`)

org_resource_download_policy.description: Which remote resources are downloaded (the images of links): `true` all of them; `"prompt"` those considered safe, and the others when the answer to Emacs's question says so; `"safe"` only those considered safe; `false` none but those. (`org-resource-download-policy`)

org_safe_remote_resources.description: The remote resources considered safe: Emacs regexps matched against a resource's URL and against the `file://` URL of the file asking for it. The answers `!`, `d` and `f` to the download question add one for the rest of the session. (`org-safe-remote-resources`)

org_startup_with_link_previews.description: Show the images of links to image files in place when a file opens, as `C-c C-x C-v` (`org.link.preview`) shows them. `#+STARTUP: inlineimages` (or `linkpreviews`) and `noinlineimages` decide for a file. Editors that can show images: Neovim from 0.13 (`vim.ui.img`), in a terminal with the Kitty graphics protocol. (`org-startup-with-link-previews`)

org_startup_with_latex_preview.description: Show the LaTeX fragments as images when a file opens, as `C-c C-x C-l` (`org.latex.preview`) shows them, made by Emacs. `#+STARTUP: latexpreview` and `nolatexpreview` decide for a file. (`org-startup-with-latex-preview`)

org_startup_indented.description: Show files indented by level without changing them (`org-indent-mode`): the text under a headline lines up with its title, and leading stars are hidden. `#+STARTUP: indent` and `noindent` decide for a file. It turns `org_adapt_indentation` off in such files, unless that is `"headline-data"`. The lines a long line wraps into go on under its text, a headline's title or an item's text (`wrap-prefix`) in Neovim and Vim, without the prefix; under the prefix in Zed and Helix. (`org-startup-indented`)

org_startup_numerated.description: Number the headlines of files (`org-num-mode`): `1`, `1.1`, `1.2`… after the stars, shown as inlay hints without changing the file. `#+STARTUP: num` and `nonum` decide for a file, and `org.num.mode` turns it on and off. (`org-startup-numerated`)

org_num_skip_footnotes.description: `org-num-mode` leaves the footnotes section (`* Footnotes`) unnumbered. (`org-num-skip-footnotes`)

org_num_skip_tags.description: `org-num-mode` leaves the subtrees of headlines with one of these tags (their own, not inherited) unnumbered. (`org-num-skip-tags`)

org_num_skip_unnumbered.description: `org-num-mode` leaves the subtrees of headlines with an `UNNUMBERED` property unnumbered. (`org-num-skip-unnumbered`)

org_hide_leading_stars.description: Hide all the stars of a headline but the last; they keep their place. `#+STARTUP: hidestars` and `showstars` decide for a file. (`org-hide-leading-stars`)

org_indent_mode_turns_on_hiding_stars.description: Where `org_startup_indented` (or `#+STARTUP: indent`) shows a file indented, hide the leading stars too, whatever `org_hide_leading_stars` says. (`org-indent-mode-turns-on-hiding-stars`)

org_indent_mode_turns_off_org_adapt_inde.description: Where a file shows indented, `org_adapt_indentation` is off (unless it is `headline-data`): new and moved text is not indented to its headline. (`org-indent-mode-turns-off-org-adapt-indentation`)

org_indent_indentation_per_level.description: How many columns a file shown indented moves each level of headlines and their text in; 0 shows them as they are. (`org-indent-indentation-per-level`)

org_duration_format.description: How durations are written (clock tables, clock lines, efforts): `"h:mm"` or `"h:mm:ss"`, or a list of units each with whether it is written when zero (`["d", false]`), with perhaps `["special", "h:mm"]` (the hours and minutes as `H:MM` after the larger units), `["special", "h:mm:ss"]`, `["special", 2]` (one unit with 2 decimals) and `"compact"` (no space between units). The units are those of `org_duration_units`. (`org-duration-format`)

org_duration_units.description: The units of durations and the minutes in each, for reading efforts and writing durations: `["d", 480]` for days of 8 hours. (`org-duration-units`)

org_fontify_done_headline.description: Show a headline marked done in the look of done headlines past its keyword (`org-headline-done`). (`org-fontify-done-headline`)

org_fontify_todo_headline.description: Show a headline marked with a keyword not done in the look of TODO headlines past its keyword (`org-headline-todo`, the token modifier `todo`). (`org-fontify-todo-headline`)

org_fontify_quote_and_verse_blocks.description: Show the lines inside quote and verse blocks in their own look (`org-quote`, `org-verse`: the token types `quote` and `verse`). (`org-fontify-quote-and-verse-blocks`)

org_custom_properties.description: The properties `org.custom.properties.toggle` (`org-toggle-custom-properties-visibility`) hides in the property drawers, and shows again: `["ID", "CUSTOM_ID"]`. Editors that can hide them: Neovim from 0.11, and Sublime Text, in a fold. (`org-custom-properties`)

org_n_level_faces.description: How many looks headlines take by level, from 1 to 8 (the token modifiers `level1` to `level8`, Org's `org-level-1` to `org-level-8`): with 4, a headline of level 5 looks as one of level 1, or as one of level 4 with `org_cycle_level_faces` off. (`org-n-level-faces`)

org_cycle_level_faces.description: Past the last look of `org_n_level_faces`, headlines take the looks of the levels from the first again; with `false`, those deeper all keep the last. (`org-cycle-level-faces`)

org_fontify_whole_heading_line.description: Show the look of a headline's level past the end of its text, to the edge of the window: for looks with a background. Editors that can show it: Neovim, Vim and VS Code (`org-lsp/lineHighlights`, VS Code's colors `org.headlineLevel1Background` and on). (`org-fontify-whole-heading-line`)

org_ellipsis.description: What a closed fold shows after its first line, such as `" ▾"`, in the highlight group `OrgLspEllipsis` (Neovim). Editors that can show it: Neovim and Vim. (`org-ellipsis`)

org_bullets_mode.description: org-bullets: the last star of each headline shows as a bullet, those of `org_bullets_bullet_list` by level, and the stars before it are hidden, as with `org_hide_leading_stars`. (`org-bullets-mode`)

org_bullets_bullet_list.description: The bullets of `org_bullets_mode`, one a level, repeating after the last. (`org-bullets-bullet-list`)

org_bullets_list_bullet.description: What `org_bullets_mode` shows in place of the `-`, `+` or `*` of an item, as org-bullets.nvim does; `false` leaves them as they are.

org_bullets_checkboxes.description: What `org_bullets_mode` shows between the brackets of a checkbox, `[ ]`, `[-]` and `[X]`, as org-bullets.nvim does; `false` leaves them as they are. A state left out keeps its default.

org_src_preserve_indentation.description: Leave the code of source blocks as it is indented when re-indenting. (`org-src-preserve-indentation`)

org_babel_tangle_lang_exts.description: By language, the extension of the file `:tangle yes` writes its blocks to, before Org's own (`emacs-lisp` → `el`): `{ "python": "py" }`. A language without one gives its name. (`org-babel-tangle-lang-exts`)

org_babel_tangle_use_relative_file_links.description: Whether the link comments of tangled files (`:comments link`) point back to the Org file by a relative path; with `false` by its whole path. (`org-babel-tangle-use-relative-file-links`)

org_babel_tangle_comment_format_beg.description: The comment before a tangled block (`:comments link`): `%link` the link back to it, `%source-name` its name, `%file` the Org file, `%start-line` the line its code starts on. (`org-babel-tangle-comment-format-beg`)

org_babel_tangle_comment_format_end.description: The comment after a tangled block, with the keys of `org_babel_tangle_comment_format_beg`. (`org-babel-tangle-comment-format-end`)

org_babel_tangle_uncomment_comments.description: Write the comments of tangled blocks as they are: not commented, and no line break after them. (`org-babel-tangle-uncomment-comments`)

org_babel_process_comment_text.description: The function the Org text of `:comments org` goes through: `org-remove-indentation` takes its common indentation away, `identity` leaves it; Emacs tangles with any other. (`org-babel-process-comment-text`)

org_babel_tangle_default_file_mode.description: In octal, the mode a symbolic `:tangle-mode` (`u+x`) changes. (`org-babel-tangle-default-file-mode`)

org_babel_tangle_remove_file_before_writ.description: Whether a file tangling writes again is deleted first: `true` always (a link to it becomes a file of its own), `false` never (a read-only file refuses), `"auto"` when it is read-only. (`org-babel-tangle-remove-file-before-write`)

org_babel_noweb_wrap_start.description: What opens a Noweb reference in a source block (`<<name>>`). (`org-babel-noweb-wrap-start`)

org_src_content_indentation.description: How far code is indented past its source block: when re-indenting, and when the code of a block edited in a file of its own (`C-c '`) is written back. Formerly `org_edit_src_content_indentation`, which is still read. (`org-src-content-indentation`)

org_agenda_span.description: How much time the agenda shows. (`org-agenda-span`)

org_agenda_start_on_weekday.description: The day a week or fortnight starts on; `false` starts it today. (`org-agenda-start-on-weekday`)

org_deadline_warning_days.description: How many days before a deadline it shows up. (`org-deadline-warning-days`)

org_scheduled_delay_days.description: How many days after its date a scheduled entry shows up. (`org-scheduled-delay-days`)

org_scheduled_past_days.description: How many days a scheduled entry that is not done keeps showing up. (`org-scheduled-past-days`)

org_modules.description: Org modules to load. `org-habit` turns habits on: entries with the `STYLE` property `habit` and a scheduled date with a repeater (`.+2d`, `.+2d/4d` for a deadline too) show in the agenda with a graph of the days they were done. `ol-man` makes `[[man:ls]]` a link to a man page (`org_man_command`). `org-ctags` follows links to the tags of a `TAGS` file, as loading it and calling `org-ctags-enable` does (`org_ctags_open_link_functions`). Others are ignored. (`org-modules`)

org_habit_graph_column.description: The column the consistency graph of a habit starts at in the agenda. (`org-habit-graph-column`)

org_habit_preceding_days.description: How many days before today a habit's graph shows. (`org-habit-preceding-days`)

org_habit_following_days.description: How many days after today a habit's graph shows. (`org-habit-following-days`)

org_habit_show_habits_only_for_today.description: Show habits only on today's date, not on future days of the agenda. (`org-habit-show-habits-only-for-today`)

org_habit_show_all_today.description: Show every habit today, even those not scheduled for today. (`org-habit-show-all-today`)

org_habit_today_glyph.description: The mark of today in a habit's graph. (`org-habit-today-glyph`)

org_habit_completed_glyph.description: The mark of a day a habit was done in its graph. (`org-habit-completed-glyph`)

org_habit_show_done_always_green.description: A day a habit was done is green in its graph even when it was done late. (`org-habit-show-done-always-green`)

org_habit_scheduled_past_days.description: How many days a habit that is not done keeps showing up. (`org-habit-scheduled-past-days`)

org_deadline_past_days.description: How many days a missed deadline keeps showing up. (`org-deadline-past-days`)

org_agenda_skip_scheduled_if_done.description: Leave out scheduled entries that are done. (`org-agenda-skip-scheduled-if-done`)

org_agenda_skip_deadline_if_done.description: Leave out deadlines of entries that are done. (`org-agenda-skip-deadline-if-done`)

org_agenda_skip_timestamp_if_done.description: Leave out timestamps of entries that are done. (`org-agenda-skip-timestamp-if-done`)

org_agenda_time_leading_zero.description: Write times with two digits for the hour (`08:00`). (`org-agenda-time-leading-zero`)

org_agenda_timegrid_use_ampm.description: Write the times of the agenda, the time grid's too, in 12-hour form (`8:00am`). (`org-agenda-timegrid-use-ampm`)

org_agenda_search_headline_for_time.description: Take a time in a headline (`Call at 15:00`) as the time of its entry. (`org-agenda-search-headline-for-time`)

org_agenda_remove_times_when_in_prefix.description: Take a time out of the headline when the prefix shows it; `beg` only one at the start of the headline. (`org-agenda-remove-times-when-in-prefix`)

org_agenda_default_appointment_duration.description: Minutes an entry with a start time and no end time lasts: the agenda shows it as a range. (`org-agenda-default-appointment-duration`)

org_agenda_remove_timeranges_from_blocks.description: Take a date range out of the headline of its lines. (`org-agenda-remove-timeranges-from-blocks`)

org_agenda_diary_sexp_prefix.description: A regexp (Emacs's syntax): what it matches of a diary sexp's text goes in front of the line, as a scheduled date's `Scheduled:` does. (`org-agenda-diary-sexp-prefix`)

org_agenda_show_inherited_tags.description: Show the inherited tags of an entry on its agenda lines: where `org_agenda_use_tag_inheritance` has them (`true`), always, never (`false`), or in these kinds of views (`agenda`, `todo`, `search`). Sorting by tag and `org_agenda_max_tags` go by the tags a line shows. (`org-agenda-show-inherited-tags`)

org_agenda_use_tag_inheritance.description: The kinds of views whose lines have inherited tags (`true`: all). Tags matches always have them. (`org-agenda-use-tag-inheritance`)

org_agenda_hide_tags_regexp.description: A regexp (Emacs's syntax): the tags it matches are not shown on agenda lines, but filters still see them. (`org-agenda-hide-tags-regexp`)

org_agenda_skip_additional_timestamps_sa.description: Once a timestamp of an entry has made a line for a day, leave out its other timestamps on that day. (`org-agenda-skip-additional-timestamps-same-entry`)

org_agenda_fontify_priorities.description: Highlight the priority cookies of agenda lines (`cookies`), or each line from its cookie on (`true`; links and tags keep their own look); the highest priority shows in bold, the lowest in italic. `false` highlights none. Org's list of faces by priority is not read here: `org_priority_faces` gives them. (`org-agenda-fontify-priorities`)

org_agenda_prefer_last_repeat.description: Show a repeating scheduled date, deadline or timestamp at its last repeat up to today instead of its base date, for every entry (`true`) or for those with one of these TODO keywords. (`org-agenda-prefer-last-repeat`)

org_agenda_skip_deadline_prewarning_if_s.description: For a scheduled entry, show its deadline only on its date (`true`), not before its scheduled date (`pre-scheduled`), or from N days before it (a number). (`org-agenda-skip-deadline-prewarning-if-scheduled`)

org_agenda_skip_scheduled_delay_if_deadl.description: For an entry with a deadline, drop the delay of its scheduled date (`--2d`) (`true`), or keep it no later than the deadline (`post-deadline`). A number drops it too, as Org's code does. (`org-agenda-skip-scheduled-delay-if-deadline`)

org_agenda_skip_scheduled_if_deadline_is.description: Leave out a scheduled date on a day its entry's deadline shows (`true`), only when it was scheduled before today (`not-today`); `repeated-after-deadline` is `org_agenda_skip_scheduled_repeats_after_deadline`. Not for habits. (`org-agenda-skip-scheduled-if-deadline-is-shown`)

org_agenda_skip_scheduled_repeats_after_.description: Leave out the repeats of a scheduled date that come after the entry's deadline. (`org-agenda-skip-scheduled-repeats-after-deadline`)

org_agenda_skip_comment_trees.description: Leave out of every view the entries of a commented subtree (`COMMENT` after the stars). (`org-agenda-skip-comment-trees`)

org_agenda_skip_archived_trees.description: Leave out of every view the entries of an archived subtree (tagged `ARCHIVE`), unless archives mode (`v a`) shows them. Org advises leaving it on and using `v a` instead. (`org-agenda-skip-archived-trees`)

org_agenda_todo_list_sublevels.description: Show in the TODO list the TODO entries below another one. Off, the list skips the subtree of each entry it shows or leaves out for a date. (`org-agenda-todo-list-sublevels`)

org_agenda_todo_ignore_with_date.description: Leave out of the TODO list the entries with an active timestamp anywhere in their text, scheduled and deadline dates too. (`org-agenda-todo-ignore-with-date`)

org_agenda_todo_ignore_scheduled.description: Leave out of the TODO list the scheduled entries: all of them (`true`, `all`), those scheduled after today (`future`), today or before (`past`), or with a number N, N days from now or later (a negative N: N days ago or before). (`org-agenda-todo-ignore-scheduled`)

org_agenda_todo_ignore_deadlines.description: Leave out of the TODO list the entries with a deadline: in its warning period, that is, shown in the agenda (`true`, `near`), not yet in it (`far`), all of them (`all`), after today (`future`), today or before (`past`), or with a number as for `org_agenda_todo_ignore_scheduled`. (`org-agenda-todo-ignore-deadlines`)

org_agenda_todo_ignore_timestamp.description: Leave out of the TODO list the entries with an active timestamp that is no scheduled or deadline date, with the values of `org_agenda_todo_ignore_scheduled`. (`org-agenda-todo-ignore-timestamp`)

org_agenda_todo_ignore_time_comparison_u.description: Compare the dates of the `org_agenda_todo_ignore_*` settings with now to the second instead of by day: `future` is then later than now, and a number counts seconds. (`org-agenda-todo-ignore-time-comparison-use-seconds`)

org_tags_match_list_sublevels.description: Whether tags matches (agenda, sparse trees) and stuck projects list the entries below one they list: `false` passes over its subtree, `indented` shows them with a dot for each level below the first. (`org-tags-match-list-sublevels`)

org_agenda_tags_todo_honor_ignore_option.description: Have the `org_agenda_todo_ignore_*` settings leave entries out of `tags-todo` matches as well. (`org-agenda-tags-todo-honor-ignore-options`)

org_agenda_sorting_strategy.description: How the lines of a day (`agenda`), the TODO list (`todo`), a tags match (`tags`, `tags-todo` too) and a search (`search`) are ordered: the strategies in turn, each deciding when the ones before do not. A view without a list takes `agenda`'s, and without that `time-up`, `category-keep`, `urgency-down`; one list alone is for every view. `time-up`/`-down` the time of day; `timestamp-`, `scheduled-`, `deadline-`, `ts-` (active) and `tsia-` (inactive) `up`/`down` the date of that kind (in the TODO list and a tags match, the entry's); `priority-` the priority, `urgency-` the priority with how near or overdue the date is; `effort-`, `category-` (and `category-keep`, the order the entries come in), `tag-` (the last tag), `todo-state-` (where the keyword is in the file's list, done ones first), `habit-`, `alpha-` (the headline), `stats-` (the statistics cookie). `user-defined-up` and `-down` call Lisp, which the server does not run. (`org-agenda-sorting-strategy`)

org_agenda_sort_notime_is_late.description: Lines without a time (or without the date a strategy sorts by) come after those with one. (`org-agenda-sort-notime-is-late`)

org_agenda_sort_noeffort_is_high.description: Entries without an effort count as having the highest when sorted, filtered or limited by effort. (`org-agenda-sort-noeffort-is-high`)

org_agenda_max_entries.description: How many entries a day of the agenda, the TODO list, a tags match or a search shows at most: one number for all, or one for each kind of view. Other lines, such as those of the time grid, go as well; with a negative number they stay. (`org-agenda-max-entries`)

org_agenda_max_todos.description: How many entries with a TODO keyword a view shows at most, the other lines going as well; with a negative number, those stay. (`org-agenda-max-todos`)

org_agenda_max_tags.description: How many entries with tags a view shows at most, the other lines going as well; with a negative number, those stay. (`org-agenda-max-tags`)

org_agenda_max_effort.description: The most minutes of effort the entries of a view add up to: entries show while their efforts, in order, stay within it (an entry without one counts as the highest, or as -1 with `org_agenda_sort_noeffort_is_high` off). (`org-agenda-max-effort`)

org_agenda_show_future_repeats.description: Show the future dates of repeating entries: all of them, none, or only the next. (`org-agenda-show-future-repeats`)

org_agenda_tags_column.description: Where tags are aligned in the agenda: a column (negative: where they end), or `auto` for the right edge of the window. With `auto`, the editors that tell the server how wide the agenda's window is (Neovim, Vim, Sublime Text) have the tags there, and the agenda follows the window as it is resized; the others (VS Code, Zed) have them end at column 80. (`org-agenda-tags-column`)

org_agenda_time_grid.description: The time grid, as Org writes it: the days that have it (`daily`: a one-day agenda; `weekly`: every day of a longer one; `today`: today; `require-timed`: only days with an entry that has a time; `remove-match`: no grid line at a time an entry already has), the times of its lines (`800` for 8:00), what follows a time that has no end time, and the text of a grid line. (`org-agenda-time-grid`)

org_agenda_current_time_string.description: The text of the line for the current time. (`org-agenda-current-time-string`)

org_agenda_show_current_time_in_grid.description: Show the current time in the grid. (`org-agenda-show-current-time-in-grid`)

org_agenda_weekend_days.description: The days drawn as the weekend (0 is Sunday). (`org-agenda-weekend-days`)

org_agenda_start_with_log_mode.description: Start the agenda in log mode, which shows what was closed and clocked each day (`l` toggles it). (`org-agenda-start-with-log-mode`)

org_agenda_start_with_clockreport_mode.description: Start the agenda with the clock report under it (`R` toggles it). (`org-agenda-start-with-clockreport-mode`)

org_agenda_clockreport_parameter_plist.description: The parameters of the clock report's table, as those of a clock table block (`:maxlevel 3 :tags t`); `:block`, `:tstart`, `:tend` and `:scope` are the agenda's. (`org-agenda-clockreport-parameter-plist`)

org_agenda_clock_report_header.description: Text on a line of its own (or lines) before the clock report. (`org-agenda-clock-report-header`)

org_agenda_start_with_archives_mode.description: Start the agenda with entries in archived trees (`trees`; `v a` toggles it), or those and the files the agenda files archive to (`files`; `v A`). (`org-agenda-start-with-archives-mode`)

org_agenda_log_mode_items.description: What log mode shows: `closed` entries, `clock` lines and `state` changes. (`org-agenda-log-mode-items`)

org_agenda_log_mode_add_notes.description: Show the note of a state change or a clock line after the headline in log mode. (`org-agenda-log-mode-add-notes`)

org_agenda_move_date_from_past_immediate.description: Moving a date of the past one day later from the agenda (`S-<right>`) takes it to today. (`org-agenda-move-date-from-past-immediately-to-today`)

org_agenda_persistent_marks.description: Keep the marks of a bulk action (`B`) after it (`p` in its menu toggles this for one action). (`org-agenda-persistent-marks`)

org_agenda_show_outline_path.description: As the cursor moves in the agenda, show where the entry of its line is: the file's name and the headlines above it (`work.org/Projects/Report`), in the echo area or the status bar. With `title` the file's `#+TITLE:` comes first instead of its name. (`org-agenda-show-outline-path`)

org_agenda_start_with_follow_mode.description: Start the agenda in follow mode, which shows the entry of the cursor's line in another window as the cursor moves (`F` toggles it). (`org-agenda-start-with-follow-mode`)

org_agenda_start_with_entry_text_mode.description: Start the agenda with some text of each entry under its line (`E` toggles it). (`org-agenda-start-with-entry-text-mode`)

org_agenda_entry_text_maxlines.description: The most lines of an entry's text `E` shows. (`org-agenda-entry-text-maxlines`)

org_agenda_entry_text_leaders.description: What each line of an entry's text starts with in the agenda. (`org-agenda-entry-text-leaders`)

org_agenda_entry_text_exclude_regexps.description: Emacs regexps whose matches are left out of the entry text `E` shows. (`org-agenda-entry-text-exclude-regexps`)

org_agenda_add_entry_text_maxlines.description: The most lines of each entry's text written under its line when the agenda is written to a plain text file (`C-x C-w`), each after four spaces and `>`; 0 writes none. The text `E` shows is not written. (`org-agenda-add-entry-text-maxlines`)

org_agenda_add_entry_text_descriptive_li.description: Whether links in the text `org_agenda_add_entry_text_maxlines` writes show as their descriptions. In Org 9.8.10 a plain text file has the links as they are either way, and so does org-lsp. (`org-agenda-add-entry-text-descriptive-links`)

org_agenda_view_columns_initially.description: Show column view (through Emacs) each time an agenda view is made, as `C-c C-x C-c` there would. (`org-agenda-view-columns-initially`)

org_agenda_persistent_filter.description: A new agenda view keeps the filters by tag, category, regexp and effort of the agenda still open, rather than starting without them. (`org-agenda-persistent-filter`)

org_agenda_block_separator.description: What goes between the blocks of a block agenda: one character repeated across 79 columns, a longer text as it is, or `false` for nothing. In a block's `settings`, the separator above that block. (`org-agenda-block-separator`)

org_agenda_compact_blocks.description: Leave out the separators between blocks and the header over agenda blocks. (`org-agenda-compact-blocks`)

agenda_hide_empty_blocks.description: Leave out the blocks of a block agenda that show no entries. Not in Org.

org_super_agenda_mode.description: org-super-agenda: show the lines of the agenda's views in the groups of `org_super_agenda_groups`, each under a header. Off, the groups are not used. (`org-super-agenda-mode`)

org_super_agenda_groups.description: org-super-agenda's groups, in turn taking the lines they select: each an object of selectors and their arguments in Emacs's order, `{ name = "Today", time-grid = true }`, or a list of them in turn; `true` is `t`, `false` is `nil` (and for `name`, `none`: no header). The lines no group takes come last, under `org_super_agenda_unmatched_name`. In a custom command's `settings`, the groups of that command or block. (`org-super-agenda-groups`)

org_super_agenda_unmatched_name.description: The header of the lines no group takes. (`org-super-agenda-unmatched-name`)

org_super_agenda_unmatched_order.description: Where the lines no group takes come among the groups: groups show lowest `order` first. (`org-super-agenda-unmatched-order`)

org_super_agenda_header_separator.description: What goes before each header: text, or one character repeated across the window, then a newline. (`org-super-agenda-header-separator`)

org_super_agenda_final_group_separator.description: What goes after the last group: text put at the end of its last line, or one character repeated across the window on a line of its own. (`org-super-agenda-final-group-separator`)

org_super_agenda_date_format.description: The headers of the groups of `auto-planning` and `auto-ts`, as `format-time-string` writes dates. (`org-super-agenda-date-format`)

org_super_agenda_hide_empty_groups.description: Leave out the headers of groups whose lines the agenda's filters all hide. (`org-super-agenda-hide-empty-groups`)

org_super_agenda_keep_order.description: Sort the lines of each group again, as the view sorts its lines: a group of several selectors puts the lines of its first selector first. (`org-super-agenda-keep-order`)

org_super_agenda_properties_inherit.description: Look for the properties of `property`, `auto-property` and `auto-group` in the entries above too. (`org-super-agenda-properties-inherit`)

org_roam_enabled.description: org-roam: the files of `org_roam_directory` are a network of notes, whose nodes (files and entries with an `ID`) are found, linked to and made with the `org.roam.*` commands. Off, those commands only say so.

org_roam_directory.description: The directory of org-roam's files, in all its subdirectories. `~/` is the home directory. (`org-roam-directory`)

org_roam_file_extensions.description: The extensions of org-roam's files; each may be followed by `.gpg` or `.age`, which the server cannot read. (`org-roam-file-extensions`)

org_roam_file_exclude_regexp.description: Emacs regexps for the files that are not org-roam's, matched against their names relative to `org_roam_directory`; the default leaves out attachments. (`org-roam-file-exclude-regexp`)

org_roam_node_display_template.description: How a node is offered: `${field}` for its `title`, `tags`, `todo`, `file`, `olp`, `aliases` and the other fields of `org-roam-node`, `${field:N}` in N columns, `${field:*}` in what is left of the window's 79 columns. (`org-roam-node-display-template`)

org_roam_node_formatter.description: The description of a link `org.roam.node.insert` makes, a template as `org_roam_node_display_template` is (`${title} (${file})`); empty for the node's title. (`org-roam-node-formatter`)

org_roam_db_extra_links_elements.description: Where else org-roam finds links than where Org does: in property drawers (`node-property`) and keyword lines (`keyword`). (`org-roam-db-extra-links-elements`)

org_roam_db_extra_links_exclude_keys.description: By `node-property` and `keyword`, the properties and keywords whose links are not links, in any case. A list given replaces the default one. (`org-roam-db-extra-links-exclude-keys`)

org_roam_graph_executable.description: The Graphviz program that draws `org.roam.graph`'s graph, found on `PATH` or a path. (`org-roam-graph-executable`)

org_roam_graph_viewer.description: The program that shows the graph, given its file. (`org-roam-graph-viewer`)

org_roam_graph_filetype.description: What Graphviz draws the graph as (its `-T`): `svg`, `png`, `pdf`… (`org-roam-graph-filetype`)

org_roam_graph_extra_config.description: Graphviz's attributes of the graph, in their order: `{ "rankdir": "LR" }`. (`org-roam-graph-extra-config`)

org_roam_graph_node_extra_config.description: Graphviz's attributes of the nodes, by the type of the link to them: `id` for org-roam's nodes, `https` for the web pages linked to. (`org-roam-graph-node-extra-config`)

org_roam_graph_link_hidden_types.description: The types of links the graph leaves out. (`org-roam-graph-link-hidden-types`)

org_roam_graph_max_title_length.description: The width a title takes in the graph, at most. (`org-roam-graph-max-title-length`)

org_roam_graph_shorten_titles.description: What becomes of a title wider than `org_roam_graph_max_title_length`: cut with `...` (`truncate`), over lines (`wrap`), or nothing (`false`). (`org-roam-graph-shorten-titles`)

org_roam_extract_new_file_path.description: The file `org.roam.extract` offers for a node, relative to `org_roam_directory`: `%<…>` is the time as `format-time-string` writes it, `${title}`, `${slug}` and `${id}` the node's. (`org-roam-extract-new-file-path`)

org_roam_link_auto_replace.description: Turn the `roam:` links of org-roam's files into `id:` links to their nodes as the files are saved, and as a link is followed. (`org-roam-link-auto-replace`)

org_roam_completion_everywhere.description: In org-roam's files, offer the titles of the nodes for the word at the cursor, not only in a link; the one picked becomes a link to its node. (`org-roam-completion-everywhere`)

org_roam_mode_sections.description: The sections of the org-roam buffer, in turn: `backlinks` (the nodes that link to the node), `reflinks` (those that link to or cite its references) and `unlinked-references` (the places that name it without a link, found by the server itself). (`org-roam-mode-sections`)

key.description: The keys that pick the template

type.description: An Org entry (the default), plain text, a list item, a checkbox item or a table line

target.description: `file` and a path; `file+head`, a path and the head of a new file; `file+olp`, a path and an outline path; `file+head+olp`, a path, a head and an outline path; or `node` and a node's title, alias or ID

prepend.description: First under the target, not last

unnarrowed.description: Show the whole file in the capture buffer

org_roam_capture_templates.description: The templates of new nodes, as `org_capture_templates` writes them, with org-roam's targets: `file` and a path, `file+head`, a path and the text a new file starts with, `file+olp`, a path and the headlines of an outline path, `file+head+olp`, both, and `node` and the title, alias or `ID` of a node. The path, relative to `org_roam_directory`, and the texts may have `${title}`, `${slug}`, `${id}` and `${name}`, which asks for `name` (`${name=default}` starts the answer with `default`), besides the escapes of `org_capture_templates`. `unnarrowed` shows the whole file in the capture buffer. (`org-roam-capture-templates`)

org_roam_dailies_directory.description: Where the daily notes are, relative to `org_roam_directory`. (`org-roam-dailies-directory`)

key.description: The keys that pick the template

type.description: An Org entry (the default), plain text, a list item, a checkbox item or a table line

target.description: `file` and a path; `file+head`, a path and the head of a new file; `file+olp`, a path and an outline path; `file+head+olp`, a path, a head and an outline path; or `node` and a node's title, alias or ID

prepend.description: First under the target, not last

unnarrowed.description: Show the whole file in the capture buffer

org_roam_dailies_capture_templates.description: The templates of the daily notes, as `org_roam_capture_templates` writes them, with paths relative to `org_roam_dailies_directory`; `%<…>` is the note's day. (`org-roam-dailies-capture-templates`)

org_journal_enabled.description: org-journal: a journal in `org_journal_dir`, a file a day (or week, month, year), written with the `org.journal.*` commands. Off, those commands only say so.

org_journal_dir.description: The directory of the journal's files. `~/` is the home directory. (`org-journal-dir`)

org_journal_file_type.description: A file a day (`daily`), week (`weekly`), month (`monthly`) or year (`yearly`); but daily, each entry has its date in a `CREATED` property. (`org-journal-file-type`)

org_journal_start_on_weekday.description: The day a weekly file starts on: 1 is Monday, 7 Sunday. (`org-journal-start-on-weekday`)

org_journal_file_format.description: The names of the files, as `format-time-string` writes the date their entries start on: with `%Y`, `%m` and `%d` (a yearly file needs only `%Y`, a monthly one `%Y` and `%m`). A name without `.org` is an Org file to org-journal, but not to most editors. (`org-journal-file-format`)

org_journal_date_format.description: The date of an entry, after `org_journal_date_prefix`, as `format-time-string` writes it, in the C locale: `%x` is `10/09/26`. (`org-journal-date-format`)

org_journal_date_prefix.description: What comes before the date of an entry: a headline, or `#+title: ` in a daily file. (`org-journal-date-prefix`)

org_journal_time_format.description: The time of a new entry of the day, as `format-time-string` writes it; empty for none. (`org-journal-time-format`)

org_journal_time_format_post_midnight.description: The time of an entry made after midnight while it is still yesterday (`org_extend_today_until`); empty for `org_journal_time_format`. (`org-journal-time-format-post-midnight`)

org_journal_time_prefix.description: What comes before the time of an entry: its stars give its level. (`org-journal-time-prefix`)

org_journal_hide_entries_p.description: Fold all but the new entry. (`org-journal-hide-entries-p`)

org_journal_follow_mode.description: In the calendar (`org.goto.calendar`), the entry of the day `]` and `[` move to shows in another window. (`org-journal-follow-mode`)

org_journal_find_file_fn.description: Where a new entry and today's file (`org.journal.open.current`) show: in another window, or (`"find-file"`) in the window of the command. (`org-journal-find-file-fn`)

org_journal_carryover_items.description: The items of the entry before that move to today's, with the headlines above them: a match of the tags view (`m`); empty for none. (`org-journal-carryover-items`)

org_journal_skip_carryover_drawers.description: Drawers left out of the items carried over. (`org-journal-skip-carryover-drawers`)

org_journal_carryover_delete_empty_journ.description: What happens to an entry or file left empty by the carryover: `never` deleted, `always`, or `ask`. (`org-journal-carryover-delete-empty-journal`)

org_journal_file_header.description: What a new file starts with, as `format-time-string` writes it: `#+title: Journal %Y`. (`org-journal-file-header`)

org_journal_created_property_timestamp_f.description: The date in the `CREATED` property of an entry of a file that is not daily. (`org-journal-created-property-timestamp-format`)

org_journal_scheduled_string.description: What comes before the timestamp of an entry for a day to come (`org.journal.new.scheduled.entry`). (`org-journal-scheduled-string`)

org_journal_enable_encryption.description: Tag the date of a new entry with `crypt`, for `org-crypt` to encrypt (`org.crypt.encrypt.all`, or as the file is saved with `org-crypt-use-before-save-magic` in the Emacs configuration). (`org-journal-enable-encryption`)

org_journal_enable_agenda_integration.description: Add the journal's files of today and the days to come to the agenda's files. (`org-journal-enable-agenda-integration`)

org_journal_search_result_date_format.description: The date of each result of a search of the journal, as `format-time-string` writes it. (`org-journal-search-result-date-format`)

org_journal_search_results_order_by.description: The order of the results of a search of the journal: `asc`, the first day first, or `desc`, the last. (`org-journal-search-results-order-by`)

org_extend_today_until.description: The hour before which it is still yesterday: for the agenda's today, the date prompt with nothing to start from, the times capture templates put in and the day of a datetree, `.+` and `++` repeaters, clock report ranges and org-journal's new entries. (`org-extend-today-until`)

org_use_effective_time.description: Before the hour `org_extend_today_until`, a TODO change records 23:59 of the day before: in `CLOSED:`, `LAST_REPEAT` and the notes' timestamps. `org.todo.yesterday` does so at any hour. (`org-use-effective-time`)

org_use_last_clock_out_time_as_effective.description: A TODO change records the end of the first closed clock of the subtree instead of the time now, when there is one; this comes before `org_use_effective_time`. (`org-use-last-clock-out-time-as-effective-time`)

org_agenda_search_view_always_boolean.description: Read every search string of the search view (`s`) as words that must (`+word`, `word`) or must not (`-word`) occur, regexps in braces (`{regexp}`) and `"quoted phrases"`. Off, it is a phrase whose spaces match any whitespace, unless its first word starts with `+`, `-` or `{`. (`org-agenda-search-view-always-boolean`)

org_agenda_search_view_force_full_words.description: The words of a Boolean search match whole words only, as a search string starting with `:` asks. (`org-agenda-search-view-force-full-words`)

org_agenda_search_view_max_outline_level.description: The search view shows headlines down to this level, a match below one counting for the headline above: 0 for every level. (`org-agenda-search-view-max-outline-level`)

org_agenda_text_search_extra_files.description: Files the search view (`s`) searches besides the agenda files, after them, as `org_agenda_files` names them. `agenda-archives` first adds the files the agenda files archive to. A file listed twice is searched at its last place. (`org-agenda-text-search-extra-files`)

org_agenda_prefix_format.description: What comes before the headline on a line of the agenda (`agenda`), the TODO list (`todo`), tags searches (`tags`) and text searches (`search`): `%c` the category, `%t` the time, `%s` the leader (`Scheduled: `), `%e` the effort, `%l` a blank per level, `%T` the last tag, `%b` the headlines above (breadcrumbs), `%i` the icon (none). A width pads (`%-12c` on the right, `%12c` on the left), `.N` cuts, `%?` leaves out an empty field, and a character before the letter follows a value that is not empty (`%-12:c`). `%(…)` is Emacs Lisp, run by Emacs (the `emacs` option) on the entry's headline with `category`, `extra`, `level` … bound, as Org runs it: `%(org-entry-get nil "X")`, or a function of `emacs_config`. Without Emacs it is empty. (`org-agenda-prefix-format`)

org_agenda_todo_keyword_format.description: How a TODO keyword is written in the agenda: `%-4s` pads it to four columns, so that the titles line up; an empty format leaves keywords out. (`org-agenda-todo-keyword-format`)

org_agenda_scheduled_leaders.description: The leader of a scheduled entry on its day, and on today when its day has passed (`%d`: the days since). (`org-agenda-scheduled-leaders`)

org_agenda_deadline_leaders.description: The leader of a deadline on its day, on today before it (`%d`: the days left), and on today after it (`%d`: the days since). (`org-agenda-deadline-leaders`)

org_agenda_deadline_faces.description: The look of a deadline in the agenda by the part of its warning time that has passed: the first whose part is no more than that, none past the last. The faces are Org's: `org-imminent-deadline` (or `org-warning`), `org-upcoming-deadline`, `org-upcoming-distant-deadline`; any other name is the plain look. (`org-agenda-deadline-faces`)

org_agenda_timerange_leaders.description: The leader of a time range within a day, and of a range over days (`%d`: which day of it, `%d`: how many days). (`org-agenda-timerange-leaders`)

org_agenda_inactive_leader.description: What goes before an inactive timestamp's line, when the agenda shows them (`[`, `v [`). (`org-agenda-inactive-leader`)

org_agenda_remove_tags.description: Leave the tags out of the agenda's lines; `prefix` only when the prefix shows a tag (`%T`). (`org-agenda-remove-tags`)

org_stuck_projects.description: What the stuck projects view (`#`) lists: the projects the match string finds whose subtree has no entry with one of the TODO keywords (`*` for any not done) or tags (`*` for any), and no match of the regexp. (`org-stuck-projects`)

org_agenda_breadcrumbs_separator.description: What goes between the headlines of `%b`. (`org-agenda-breadcrumbs-separator`)

org_agenda_format_date.description: How the agenda writes a day, as `format-time-string` does: `%A %d %B %Y`, `%a %Y-%m-%d`. (`org-agenda-format-date`)

org_agenda_start_day.description: The day the agenda starts from, as the date prompt reads it: `-1d`, `+2d`, `2026-10-01`. (`org-agenda-start-day`)

key.description: The keys the context is about

use.description: The keys whose template or command these keys stand for where the context holds

contexts.description: Rules, each a regexp on the file, the mode or the buffer's name; the context holds where one of them does

org_agenda_custom_commands_contexts.description: Where the commands of `org_agenda_custom_commands` are offered, as for `org_capture_templates_contexts`. (`org-agenda-custom-commands-contexts`)

key.description: The keys that pick the command in the agenda menu

match.description: For todo, keywords (NEXT|WAIT); for tags, a match string (work-home, PRIORITY="A")

header.description: Replaces the view's header; empty for none

settings.description: Agenda options for this command: org_agenda_span, org_agenda_start_day…

blocks.description: Views shown one after the other

match.description: For todo, keywords; for tags, a match string

header.description: Replaces the view's header; empty for none

settings.description: Agenda options for this block: org_agenda_span, org_agenda_start_day…

org_agenda_custom_commands.description: Commands of the agenda menu. Each has a `key` and a `description`, and either a `type` (`agenda`, `alltodo`, `todo`, `tags` or `tags-todo`) with a `match` (keywords such as `NEXT|WAIT` for `todo`, a match string such as `work-home` or `PRIORITY="A"` for `tags`), or `blocks`, a list of such views shown one after the other. `header` replaces a view's header (empty: none), and `settings` holds agenda options for the command or a block (`org_agenda_span`, `org_agenda_start_day` …). A command with only a key and a description groups the commands whose keys start with its key. (`org-agenda-custom-commands`)
